[1] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 85 · 7.5.3.3 Re-greasing intervals
Rolling bearings of electrical machines need to be re-greased at regular intervals. The re-greasing interval is found on the bearing plate.
NOTE:
Regardless of the re-greasing interval, the bearings need to be re-greased at least once per year.
The re-greasing intervals are calculated for an operating temperature of 70°C (160°F). If the operating temperature is lower or higher than the assumed, the re-grease interval has to be altered accordingly. Higher operating temperature decreases the re-greasing interval.
NOTE:
An increase in the ambient temperature raises the temperature of the bearings correspondingly. The values for the re-greasing interval should be halved for every 15°C (30°F) increase in bearing temperature and may be once doubled for a 15°C (30°F) decrease in bearing temperature.

[2] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 74 · 7.3 Maintenance program
This chapter presents a recommended maintenance program for ABB machines. This maintenance program is of a general nature, and should be considered as a minimum level of maintenance. Maintenance should be intensified when local conditions are demanding or very high reliability is required. It should also be noted that even when following this maintenance program, normal supervision and observation of the machine's condition is required.
Please note that even though the maintenance programs below have been customized to match the machine, it might contain references to accessories not available on all machines.
The maintenance program is based on four levels of maintenance, which rotate according to operating hours. The amount of work and down time vary, so that level 1 includes mainly quick visual inspections and level 4 more demanding measurements and replacements. More information about the spare part packages suitable for these maintenances can be found in Chapter 9.2 Spare parts for rotating electrical machines. The recommended maintenance interval can be seen in Table 6 Maintenance intervals. The operation hour recommendation in this chapter is given as equivalent operating hours (Eq. h), that can be counted by the following formula:

[3] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 66 · Figure 32 Example of lubrication channel through bearing arrangement of horizontal machine
NOTE:
NOTE:
Start-up greasing may take several grease portions (3-10 times amount mentioned at the lubrication plate).
The re-lubrication interval will never be longer than 12 months.
The type of original grease used is found on the bearing plate on the machine. Acceptable types of grease can be found in Chapter 7.5.3 Rolling bearings.
NOTE:
Do not mix greases! There must be only one type of grease inside the bearing - not mixture of two or more greases.
The temperature of the bearings will initially increase because of the excess grease. After few hours, the excess grease will be discharged through the lubrication valve and the temperature of the bearing will return to normal running temperature.
If available, and after the machine has been running for several hours, measure the vibrations or SPM-values from the SPM-nipples, and record the values for future reference use.
Following chapter for bearing type: Sleeve bearing

[4] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 69 · 6.4 Supervision
The operating personnel should inspect the machine at regular intervals. This means that they should listen, feel and smell the machine and its associated equipment in order to obtain a feeling for normal operating condition.
The object of the supervision inspection is to familiarize the personnel with the equipment. This is essential in order to detect and fix abnormal occurrences in time.
The safety precautions shown in the Safety Instructions must be observed at all times.
The difference between supervision and maintenance is rather diffuse. Normal supervision of operation includes logging of operating data such as load, temperatures and vibrations. This data is useful basis for maintenance and service.
- During the first period of operation (- 200 hours) supervision should be intensive. Temperatures of bearings and windings, load, current, cooling, lubrication and vibration shall be checked frequently.
- During the following duty period (200 - 1000 hours), a check-up once a day is sufficient. A record of supervision inspections should be filed and saved for further reference. The time between inspections may be extended if the operation is continuous and stable.
For relevant check-lists, see Appendix Commissioning report.

results.answer:
The tightening torque for an M20 strength class 8.8 standard-thread screw on the Kohler KD27V12 engine is 390 Nm.

| Standard thread - Strength class | Tightening torque - 8.8 |

The condition for applying this torque is the use of metric standard threads classified as 8.8, which is commonly used in such applications to ensure proper fastening and avoid loosening under operational conditions. There are no additional specific procedures or values mentioned that would modify this standard torque value in the context provided. 

The information comes from the Kohler Generator Manual [1].

results.answer:
The cold inlet and outlet valve clearances for the Kohler KD27V12 are as follows:

| Valve Type            | Clearance (mm) | Clearance (in) |
|-----------------------|----------------|-----------------|

These values are listed in the manual under the section for cylinder head specifications [1]. 

For adjusting the valve clearances, follow this procedure:

1. Ensure the engine is cold.
2. Remove the valve cover.
3. Use a feeler gauge to measure the clearance at the specified points.
4. If the clearance is not within the specified range, adjust the valve lash as needed.
5. Reassemble the valve cover and startup the engine for a test run to ensure proper operation. 

The specified clearance values are important for maintaining optimal engine performance and efficiency. If there's an error in the valve clearance, it can lead to engine knocking [4].

The machine is equipped with temperature detectors to be connected to a temperature monitoring and protection system. The location and type, as well as the settings for these detectors, can be found on the dimensional drawing, and the connection diagram of the machine.
The temperature alarm level for resistance temperature detectors (RTD, Pt-100) should be set as low as possible. The level can be determined based on the test results, or the noticed operating temperature. The temperature alarm can be set 10K (20°F) higher than the operating temperature of the machine during maximal load at highest ambient temperature.
If a two-function temperature monitoring system is used, the lower level is normally used as an alarm level and the higher as a trip level.
NOTE:
In case the machine trips, the reason must be found and eliminated before the machine is restarted. In case of an alarm, find the reason and correct the situation. Use the trouble shooting guide, see Chapter 8.1 Trouble shooting.

The temperatures of the bearings, stator windings and cooling air should be checked when the machine is running.
The winding and bearing temperature may not reach a stable temperature until after several (4-8) hours, when running at full load.
The stator winding temperature depends on the load of the machine. If full load cannot be obtained during or soon after commissioning, the present load and temperature should be noted and included in the commissioning report.

results.question: If the fuel sulfur content is between 0.5% and 1%, how does the Kohler engine oil change interval change?
results.expected_answer: Oil change factor 1/2 — the interval is halved; limited to engine oil categories 2 and 3
results.rewritten_query: What is the impact of 0.5% to 1% fuel sulfur content on the oil change interval for Kohler engines?
results.answer:
The oil change interval for a Kohler engine will be reduced by half if the fuel sulfur content is between 0.5% and 1%. This is indicated by the oil change factor of "1/2" for this range of sulfur content.

Here are the relevant details regarding the change interval:

| Sulfur content in % | Oil change factor (factor 2) |
| - | - |
| 0.5 < Sulfur content ≤ 1 | "1/2" => reduces the maintenance interval by half |

### Likely Reasons for the Change
- The presence of sulfur in the fuel can lead to increased engine wear and the formation of harmful combustion gases, necessitating more frequent oil changes to maintain engine performance and longevity.

### Procedure for Adjusting Oil Change Interval
1. Determine the basic oil change interval from the maintenance tables for the genset application and engine type.
2. Identify the sulfur content of the fuel being used.
3. Apply the oil change interval factor based on the sulfur content:
   - For sulfur content between 0.5% and 1%, multiply the basic change interval by the factor of 0.5.
4. Consider validating the oil change interval through engine oil analysis if any difficulty factors or more challenging operating conditions are present. 

Refer to the specific maintenance schedule for further details on the intervals and required actions based on the engine's operational context.

results.question: According to the Kohler KD27V12 manual, what permissible average power output over 24 hours applies to an ESP-rated and a PRP-rated generator?
results.source: 5.2.1 Nominal values of the power generator, p.49
results.expected_answer: ESP: not above 85% of the ESP rating (up to 200 h/year); PRP: not above 75% of the PRP rating
results.rewritten_query: What is the permissible average power output over 24 hours for an ESP-rated and a PRP-rated generator according to the Kohler KD27V12 manual?
results.answer:
The permissible average power output over 24 hours for an ESP-rated generator is up to 85 percent of the ESP rating, and for a PRP-rated generator, it is up to 75 percent of the PRP rating.

### Permissible Average Power Output

| Generator Type | Permissible Average Power Output |
|----------------|----------------------------------|
| ESP            | Up to 85% of ESP rating          |
| PRP            | Up to 75% of PRP rating          |

The permissible average power outputs are constrained by the operational conditions and maintenance practices, which must adhere to manufacturer instructions [[1]][[2]].

The maximum available power during a variable power sequence under the specified operating conditions, which a power generator is capable of delivering in the event of a power failure or under test conditions for up to 200 hours of operation per year, wherein the maintenance intervals and work are executed in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions. The maximum power that a power generator is capable of delivering continuously for an unlimited number of hours per year under the agreed operating conditions with a variable electrical load, wherein the maintenance intervals and work are executed in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions. The permissible average power output during 24 hours of operation should not exceed 75 percent of the PRP rating.

results.question: In the EMSA hydrometer test, which specific density readings indicate a fully charged, a half charged and a discharged battery?
results.rewritten_query: What specific density readings in the EMSA hydrometer test indicate fully charged, half charged, and discharged lead-acid batteries?
results.answer:
The specific density readings for the EMSA hydrometer test are as follows:

| Battery Charge Status | Specific Density |
|-----------------------|------------------|
| Fully Charged         | 1.270 - 1.280    |
| Half Charged          | 1.220 - 1.230    |
| Discharged            | 1.150 - 1.220    |

These ranges indicate the state of charge of the battery, with higher densities corresponding to a fuller charge level and lower densities indicating a more discharged state. This evaluation helps in determining the battery's charge status during maintenance checks or routine assessments of performance and health in diesel generator operations [1].

[3] Nidec Motor Manual, p. 22 · Delta Connected Motor:
Using an ohmmeter, identify the three groups of three leads. Separate these groups by tying them with tape. Attach leads to a pair of wires in a group, and observe the voltage drop from each pair of energized leads to the third lead in that group. Continue until a combination is found that gives a voltage drop from each of the energized leads to the third lead equal to one half of the battery voltage. The lead located halfway between the other two will thus be the corner lead of the delta. Repeat this for each group of leads, marking the corner leads #1, #2, and #3.
Next, use the inductive kick test method to identify the proper markings for the other two leads of each group. The two coils #3 & #6 and 3 & #8, acting in parallel, will produce the effect of a coil positioned halfway between the actual position of the two coils. The flux produced by #3 & #6 and #3 & #8 combined, will be perpendicular to the axis of #1 & #4 and #2 & #7. Opening and closing a switch in this circuit will produce a kick in coils #1 & #9 and #2 & #5, but no kick in #1 & #4 and #2 & #7.
Therefore, if the battery is connected from #3 & #6 and #3 & #8 as shown, opening and closing the battery circuit, the voltmeter will identify leads #1, #4, and #9 and can be distinguished by noting the magnitude rather than the polarity. The voltmeter can then be connected to terminal #2 for determination of the leads #5 & #7. Leads #2 to #7 will give little or no deflection, and leads #2 to #5 will give a substantial
deflection.
In succession, the battery is then transferred to the corner of #1. Tie the battery between leads #1 & #4 & #9. Making and breaking the circuit will be perpendicular to #3 & #8 and #2 & #5, resulting in no deflection. However, there will be a deflection from leads #2 & #7 and #3 & #6. Placing the battery next on the #2 & #5 and #2 & #7 leads will be perpendicular to #1 & #9 and #3 & #6 leads, therefore creating no deflection. Leads #1 & #4 and #3 & #8 would then have a deflection, thus concluding the lead testing of
the nine lead delta connected motor.

results.question: What torque does EMSA specify for the charge generator pivot bolt and connecting bolt after adjusting the belt?
results.rewritten_query: What is the specified torque for the charge generator pivot bolt and connecting bolt after belt adjustment according to EMSA?
results.answer:
The specified torque for the charge generator pivot bolt and connecting bolt after adjusting the belt is **22 Nm (16 lb ft)**[1]. 

### Procedure for Adjusting Belt Tension:
1. Loosen the pivot bolt of the charge generator.
2. Loosen the connecting bolt.
3. Move the alternator to increase or decrease the belt tension.
4. Tighten the charge generator pivot bolt and connecting bolt to **22 Nm (16 lb ft)**.

| Specification                               | Value  |
|---------------------------------------------|--------|
| Recommended Pipe Diameter                   | 1 1/2" |
| Maximum Length of the Fuel Pipe             | 6 m    |
| Maximum Vertical Height                      | 0.9 m  |

According to the provided information, these recommendations ensure adequate fuel flow and pressure for the generator's operation, allowing for proper functioning without the risk of fuel supply issues or engine damage. It is important to adhere to these specifications to maintain optimal performance and safety of the generator system. 

Ensure that the installation follows these guidelines to prevent operational problems related to fuel supply and pressure.

results.question: When adding electrolyte to an EMSA maintenance-type battery for the first time, what density and level are required, and how long is the minimum charge?
results.expected_answer: Specific density 1.280 at 20°C, filled to 15 mm above the plates (electrolyte above 10°C); minimum charging period 6 hours
results.rewritten_query: What is the required electrolyte density and level for an EMSA maintenance-type battery during initial filling, and what is the minimum charging duration?
results.answer:
To add electrolyte to an EMSA maintenance-type battery for the first time, the following steps must be followed:

1. **Fill the Battery**: Add distilled water to the battery until the electrolyte level is 10 mm above the plates.
2. **Hydrometer Test**: Check the specific density using a hydrometer to ensure it is at the following levels:
   - Fully charged: 1.270 - 1.280
   - Half charged: 1.220 - 1.230
   - Discharged: 1.150 - 1.220
3. **Charge Duration**: Allow the battery to charge for a minimum of 1 hour and check the electrolyte level again. If no change is observed after 1 hour, it is considered fully charged.

The required specific density and levels during these steps ensure the proper functioning of the battery and its maintenance [1][2][3].

[2] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 57 · 4.3.5 Insulation distances of main power connections
The connections of the main power cables must be designed to withstand demanding operation conditions where the insulators can be subjected to dirt, humidity and surge voltages. In order to ensure lasting and trouble-free running, it is therefore important that the length of the insulation and creepage distances are sufficient. The minimum insulation and creepage distances should be equal or exceed demands set by:
- Local requirements
- Standards
- Classification rules
- Hazardous area classification.
The insulation and creepage distances apply both for insulation distances between two different phases, and for insulation distances between one phase and earth. The air insulation distance is the shortest distance through air between two points with different electrical potential (voltage). The surface creepage distance is the shortest distance along surfaces next to each other between two points with different electrical potential (voltage).

The main power cable connections should be tightened correctly to ensure reliable operation. For details, see Appendix Typical main power cable connections.

[2] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 86 · Automatic re-greasing
A variety of automatic re-lubrication systems is available on the market. However, ABB recommends only the use of electromechanical re-lubrication systems. The quality of the grease entering the bearing has to be checked at least once per year: the grease has to look and feel like new grease. Any separation of the base oil from the soap is not acceptable.
NOTE:
If an automatic re-greasing system is used, double the amount of grease indicated on the bearing plate.

[3] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 66 · Figure 32 Example of lubrication channel through bearing arrangement of horizontal machine
NOTE:
NOTE:
Start-up greasing may take several grease portions (3-10 times amount mentioned at the lubrication plate).
The re-lubrication interval will never be longer than 12 months.
The type of original grease used is found on the bearing plate on the machine. Acceptable types of grease can be found in Chapter 7.5.3 Rolling bearings.
NOTE:
Do not mix greases! There must be only one type of grease inside the bearing - not mixture of two or more greases.
The temperature of the bearings will initially increase because of the excess grease. After few hours, the excess grease will be discharged through the lubrication valve and the temperature of the bearing will return to normal running temperature.
If available, and after the machine has been running for several hours, measure the vibrations or SPM-values from the SPM-nipples, and record the values for future reference use.
Following chapter for bearing type: Sleeve bearing

[4] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 84 · 7.5.2.5 Oil change schedule for mineral oils
For self-lubricated bearings cleaning intervals with oil changes of approximately 8000 operating hours are recommended and approx. 20000 operating hours for bearings with oil circulation systems.
Shorter oil change intervals may be necessary in case of frequent start-ups, high oil temperatures or excessively high contamination due to external influences.
The correct oil change interval can be found on the bearing plate and dimensional drawing, see Chapter 2.1.2 Bearing plate.
Following chapter for bearing type: Rolling bearing

[5] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 86 · 7.5.3.5 Bearing grease (table)
It is essential to use grease of good quality and with the correct base soap. This will ensure a long and trouble free lifetime of the bearings.
Grease used for re-greasing should have the following properties:
- Be special rolling bearing grease.
- Be of good quality with a lithium complex soap, and with mineral-, or PAO-oil.
- Have a base oil viscosity of 100 to 160 cSt at 40°C (105°F).
- Have a consistency NLGI grade between 1.5 and 3. For vertically or in hot conditions mounted machines, NLGI grade 2 or 3 is recommended.
- Have a continuous temperature range between -30°C (-20°F) and at least +120°C (250°F).
Grease with the correct properties is available from all major lubricant manufacturers. If the make of grease is changed and compatibility is uncertain, consult the manufacturing ABB factory, see Chapter 9.1.3 Contact information for Motors and Generators Service.
| NOTE: | Do not mix greases! There must be only one type of grease inside the bearing - not a mixture of two or more greases. |
| - | - |
| NOTE: | Grease additives are recommended. However, a written guarantee should be obtained from the lubricant manufacturer stating that the additives do not damage the bearings or the properties of the grease in the field of the operating temperature. This is especially important for EP additives. |
| NOTE: | Lubricants containing EP admixtures are not recommended. |

If unit has been in operation for several years the old grease can harden. If this occurs remove bolts holding bottom inside end cap, raise end cap and wipe out hardened grease. Reassemble and add a small amount of fresh grease.

results.question: According to the Kohler KD27V12 manual's TBN chart (Fig. 27), below what TBN should the engine oil be exchanged as soon as possible?
results.rewritten_query: What is the minimum TBN value from the Kohler KD27V12 manual's TBN chart (Fig. 27) at which engine oil should be exchanged immediately?
results.answer:
According to the Kohler KD27V12 manual's TBN chart (Fig. 27), the engine oil should be exchanged as soon as possible if the TBN is below 8 mg KOH/g.

### Likely Causes or Reasoning:
- A low TBN indicates that the oil's ability to neutralize acids is diminishing, which can be influenced by the sulfur content in the fuel. As sulfur levels increase, the required TBN levels for effective lubrication and acid neutralization also increase.

### Procedure:
1. **Monitor TBN Levels**: Regularly test the engine oil to determine its TBN value.
2. **Evaluate Sulfur Content**: Assess the sulfur content in the fuel being used.
3. **Determine Action**: 
   - If the TBN falls below 8 mg KOH/g, plan an immediate oil change.
4. **Document Findings**: Record the TBN level and any relevant observations about engine performance and fuel sulfur content.

The TBN values relevant to oil changes are as follows:

| TBN Level (mg KOH/g) | Action                               |
|-----------------------|--------------------------------------|
| < 8                   | Exchange oil as soon as possible     |

This information is derived from [1][4].

results.question: Per NEMA MG1 as listed in the Siemens vertical motor manual, what is the unfiltered vibration limit for a resiliently mounted motor at 1800 RPM?
results.rewritten_query: What is the unfiltered vibration limit for a resiliently mounted motor at 1800 RPM according to NEMA MG1, as referenced in the Siemens vertical motor manual?
results.answer:
The unfiltered vibration limit for a resiliently mounted motor at 1800 RPM, according to NEMA MG1 as listed in the Siemens vertical motor manual, is 0.15 in/s (3.8 mm/s) [1].

For ensuring proper operation, follow these steps:

1. After tightening the flange mounting bolts, check the end play.
2. Run the unit at a minimum load.
3. Measure the vibration levels.

If the measured vibration exceeds the limit, proceed to:

- Loosen the flange mounting bolts and shift within the mounting flange clearance.
- If vibration remains excessive and the unit is coupled to a load, check for:
  - Shaft alignment
  - System reed frequency

The vibration limit at 1800 RPM is critical to prevent excessive wear and ensure reliable motor performance.

[5] Nidec Motor Manual, p. 39 · Machine Mounting
Question: Does a machine's mounting style affect its vibration?
Answer: Yes. When evaluating the vibration of electrical machines, it is important to understand the machine's mounting because mounting and vibration are closely linked. Two passive (admit insignificant external disturbances to the machine) methods of mounting a motor are resilient mounting and rigid mounting. Following is a brief description of each, and an explanation of their affect on vibration.
Resilient Mounting: Resilient mounting entails suspending the machine on a spring, or mounting it on some type of elastic support (rubber, springs, etc.). Natural oscillation frequencies of the suspension system and machine should be less than 25 percent of the frequency corresponding to the lowest speed of the machine under test. The effective mass of the elastic support should be no greater than 10 percent of that of the machine, in order to reduce the influence of the mass and the moments of inertia of these parts on the vibration level.
Rigid Mounting: Rigid mounting entails fastening the machine directly to a relatively massive foundation. According to NEMA MG17.06, a relatively massive foundation is one that has a vibration which is limited, during testing, to 0.02 in/s peak (0.5 mm/s peak) above any background vibrations. The horizontal and vertical natural frequencies of the complete test arrangement shall not coincide within +10 percent of the rotational frequency of the machine, within +5 percent of two times the rotational frequency, or within +5 percent of oneand two- times the electrical-line frequency.

results.question: For a Siemens vertical motor with a solid shaft, what total indicator readings are acceptable for parallel and angular alignment?
results.expected_answer: Parallel: total indicator reading not over 0.002 inches; angular: not over 0.002 in. per foot of radius to the dial indicator
results.rewritten_query: What are the acceptable total indicator readings for parallel and angular alignment of a Siemens vertical motor with a solid shaft?
results.answer:
For a Siemens vertical motor with a solid shaft, the acceptable total indicator readings for alignment are as follows:

| Alignment Type     | Acceptable Reading              |
|---------------------|---------------------------------|
| Parallel Alignment   | Not to exceed 0.002 inches     |
| Angular Alignment    | Not to exceed 0.002 in./ft. radius at the dial indicator |

### Procedure for Checking Alignment
1. Set the indicator dial to zero at the starting point.
2. Slowly turn both coupling halves a complete turn.
3. Observe the dial reading at 90-degree increments from the starting point.
4. Check that the total indicator readings do not exceed the specified limits for parallel and angular alignment as outlined above.

Acceptable conditions are critical to avoid misalignment issues that could lead to operational inefficiency or equipment damage. It's important to follow these guidelines during the alignment process to ensure long-term reliability of the motor system. 

Refer to the alignment procedures and specifications from the documented source for detailed instructions.

The following checking procedure applies to a unit consisting of motor/generator, coupling, and a driven/drive component. Although applicable to most types of couplings, it is primarily intended for the rabbet-fit type. For other types, where the procedures differ, refer to the coupling manufacturer's Installation and Maintenance Instructions.
Work in one plane at a time and test for parallel or angular alignment with a dial indicator mounted as shown in Figure 1. Proceed as follows:
1. Set indicator dial to zero, at starting point.
2. Slowly turn both coupling halves a complete turn.
3. Observe dial reading at 90 degree increments from starting point.
4. Acceptable parallel alignment occurs when the total indicator readings do not exceed 0.002 inches.
5. Acceptable angular alignment occurs when the total indicator readings do not exceed 0.002 in./ft. radius to dial indicator.

Hollow shaft units require accurate alignment with respect to the unit shaft and the driven/drive equipment shaft. The pump shaft acts as a pendulum supported by the top coupling and unit bearing.
Align the unit as follows:
1. Clamp dial indicator to pump shaft, align with basebolt plane and set dial indicator to zero (Figure 2).
2. Remove top cover and rotate both unit and pump shafts.
3. Read dial indicator at 90 degree increments from starting point.

[1] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 5 · Temporary Storage
If the equipment is not to be installed and operated soon after arrival, store it in a clean, dry, well- ventilated place, free from vibration and rapid or wide variations in temperature. Rotate the shaft a minimum of 10 complete turns by hand each month to coat the bearings with lubricant which will retard oxidation or corrosion, and prevent possible false brinelling. If drain plugs are provided in enclosed motors, they must be removed periodically to drain any water accumulation from the motor. Consider a unit in storage when:
1. It has been delivered to the job site and is awaiting installation.
2. It has been installed but operation is delayed over 30 days pending completion of plant construction.
3. There are long (30 day) periods between operating cycles.
4. The plant (or department) is shut down for 30 days.
5. Energize space heaters, if supplied.

[2] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 20 · Maintenance
For best results, grease should be compounded of a polyurea type and a good grade of petroleum oil and stabilized against oxidation.
The frequency of relubricating bearings and the amount added each time depends on two factors - speed and service.
All grease lube bearing motors will have affixed a plate with lubricating instructions. The instructions on this plate should be followed to achieve optimum bearing life and to avoid consequential damage to rotating parts.
Relubricate with the type of grease specified on the lubrication plate mounted on the motor, or compatible grease. Mixing of non-compatible greases can cause bearing failure.
Relubricate bearings with the proper grade of grease as follows:
1. Stop the motor and lock out the switch.
2. Thoroughly clean the grease inlet fitting or plug. If the motor has a plug, remove plug and clean the inlet.
3. Remove the drain plug (and overflow plug, if so equipped) and clean out any hardened grease.
4. Slowly pump the correct amount of grease into the grease inlet, per the lubrication plate mounted on the motor. Replace inlet plug (and overflow plug, if so equipped).
5. Start motor and allow to run at least one (1) hour to expel any excess grease from the drain opening before re-installing the drain plug.
6. Stop the motor and lock out the switch.
7. Re-install the drain plug.
8. Put the motor back in operation.

[3] Nidec Motor Manual, p. 29 · Lubrication Instructions
Question: How can motors in service be relubricated?
Answer Units are pre-lubricated at the factory and do not require initial lubrication. Relubricating interval depends upon speed, type of bearing and service. Refer to table in the Operating and Instruction Manual provided with motor for suggested re-greasing intervals and recommended greases. Operating conditions may dictate more frequent lubrication. Motor must be at rest and electrical controls should be locked open to prevent energizing while motor is being serviced (refer to section on Safety). If motor is being taken out of storage, refer to storage procedures.
To re-lubricate bearings, remove the drain plug. Inspect grease drain and remove any blockage with a mechanical probe taking care not to damage bearing. Under no circumstances should a mechanical probe be used while the motor is in operation. Add new grease at the grease inlet. New grease must be compatible with grease already in the motor (refer to Table 1 in Operating & Maintenance Manual for replenishment quantities). Run the motor for 15 to 30 minutes with the drain plug removed to allow purging of any excess grease. Shut off unit and replace the drain plug. Return motor to service.

[4] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 20 · NOTE
If unit has been in operation for several years the old grease can harden. If this occurs remove bolts holding bottom inside end cap, raise end cap and wipe out hardened grease. Reassemble and add a small amount of fresh grease.
If machine is a totally-enclosed or weather-protected type disassembly of the lower bearing may be required to remove old grease. Also clean and refill inlet, overflow, and drain grease pipes.
Because the lower bearing is single shielded, the grease will not pass through the drain port unless the motor is run for some time.

results.question: What kind of grease does Siemens recommend for the bearings of its vertical induction motors?
results.expected_answer: A polyurea-type grease compounded with a good grade of petroleum oil and stabilized against oxidation (or the grease on the lubrication plate)
results.rewritten_query: What grease does Siemens recommend for vertical induction motor bearings?
results.answer:
Siemens recommends using a polyurea type grease compounded with a good grade of petroleum oil for the bearings of its vertical induction motors, according to the lubrication plate mounted on the motor. It is also important to follow the relubrication instructions affixed to the motor to achieve optimum bearing life and avoid potential damage to rotating parts. 

**Key Considerations:**
- Ensure the grease is compatible with that specified on the lubrication plate to prevent bearing failure due to mixing non-compatible greases. 

### Procedure for Greasing Bearings:
1. Stop the motor and lock out the switch.
2. Thoroughly clean the grease inlet fitting or plug. If the motor has a plug, remove it and clean the inlet.
3. Remove the drain plug (and overflow plug, if equipped) and clean out any hardened grease.
4. Slowly pump the correct amount of grease into the grease inlet, per the lubrication plate mounted on the motor. Replace the inlet plug (and overflow plug, if equipped).
5. Start the motor and allow it to run for at least one (1) hour to expel any excess grease from the drain opening before re-installing the drain plug.
6. Stop the motor and lock out the switch.
7. Re-install the drain plug.
8. Put the motor back in operation.

Adhering to these steps ensures proper lubrication and maintenance of the motor's bearings, supporting their long-term performance and reliability. [1][5]

results.question: When drying a Siemens vertical motor's stator by circulating direct current, how much current and DC voltage are usually needed?
results.expected_answer: Usually 50 to 100% of full load current; the DC voltage is 0.25–5.0% of normal voltage per phase (0.50–3.25% of the rating in power)
results.rewritten_query: What is the recommended DC current and voltage for drying a Siemens vertical motor's stator using direct current circulation?
results.answer:
To dry a Siemens vertical motor's stator by circulating direct current, the required current is usually between 50 to 100% of the full load current. The DC voltage needed for this current will be 0.25 - 5.0% of the normal voltage per phase [1].

### Summary of Required Values
| Parameter             | Value                      |
|-----------------------|----------------------------|
| Current               | 50 - 100% of full load current |
| DC Voltage            | 0.25 - 5.0% of normal voltage per phase |

### Drying Procedure
1. Remove bearing housings.
2. Center the rotor in the stator core.
3. Wedge fiber strips into the lower part of the air gap so the rotor does not touch the stator core, or remove the rotor.
4. Direct a fan on the unit to blow away excessive moisture.
5. Attach temperature indicators to windings.
6. Ensure that the temperature does not exceed the drying temperatures in the Insulation Drying Temperature table.
7. Use an external source of current to circulate direct current through the winding [2].

May cause damage to insulation.
Avoid hot spots and radiant type heat When this method is used on the stator, the stator phases may be connected in series or in parallel to suit the available power supply if both ends of all phases are accessible. If only three leads are brought out of the motor, the current may be circulated between one terminal and the other two connected together. If this is done, the temperature of the single lead connection must be checked frequently, and it is desirable to shift the leads occasionally. Usually 50 to 100% of full load current will produce the required temperature. The dc voltage required for this current will be 0.25 - 5.0% of the normal voltage per phase, and the corresponding power will be 0.50 - 3.25% of the rating.
Alternating current can be used on the stators of squirrel cage induction motors if the rotors are removed. Alternating current is usually not as easy to control as required voltage control, and a.c. requires a higher voltage source, approximately 10 to 30% of the rated winding voltage. In addition, care must be taken that miscellaneous parts adjacent to the windings, such as lead studs, core supporting member, etc., do no overheat due to induced currents and the lack of normal ventilation.
May cause damage to insulation.
Avoid hot spots and radiant type heat

[2] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 19 · Circulating Current Drying
1. Remove bearing housings.
2. Center the rotor in the stator core.
3. Wedge fiber strips into the lower part of the air gap so rotor does not touch stator core, or remove rotor.
4. Direct fan on unit to blow away excessive moisture.
5. Attach temperature indicators to windings. Do not exceed the drying temperatures in the Insulation Drying Temperature table.
6. An external source of current can be used to circulate direct current through the winding of any type of alternating current motor. A portable low voltage motor-generator set, such as is used for welding, is usually suitable.

[3] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 19 · Electric Strip Heater Drying
1. Remove bearing housings.
2. Remove rotor.
3. Direct a fan on stator to carry away the moisture.
4. Attach temperature indicators to winding and apply heat as specified in the Insulation Drying Temperature table and follow procedures described for drying insulation.
5. Radiant type heaters are not recommended because some parts may become scorched before remote parts reach desired temperature.

[4] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 16 · Maintenance Checklist
1. Verify motor is clean and verify that stator and rotor ventilation passages are unobstructed.
2. Check for excessive loading or service factor.
3. Verify winding temperature rise not in excess of rated value.
4. Verify insulation resistance is above recommended minimum.
5. Verify voltage and frequency variation.
6. Check air gap.
7. Verify that bearing temperatures are within limits and that lubricant is clean and proper level maintained.
8. Verify no unusual vibration or noise exists.
9. Check alignment.
10. Check for proper lubrication.
A definite schedule of preventive maintenance inspections should be established to avoid breakdown, serious damage and extensive downtime. The schedule will depend on operating conditions and experience with similar equipment. To assure adequate maintenance, and warranty consideration, it is essential that complete records be kept for each motor including description and rating, maintenance schedule and repairs required or carried out.
This checklist does not represent an exhaustive survey of maintenance steps necessary to ensure safe operation of this equipment. Particular applications may require further procedures. Should further information be desired or should particular problems arise which are not covered sufficiently for the purchaser's purposes, the matter should be referred to the local Siemens Sales Office.
Improper maintenance can cause death, serious injury or property damage.
Use only factory authorized parts for repair of equipment. Maintenance should be performed only by qualified personnel.

[5] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 94 · 7.6.5 Insulation resistance measurement for auxiliaries
To ensure correct operation of the machines protections and other auxiliaries, their condition can be determined by an insulation resistance test. results.question: How should MICLAD VPI stator coils on a Siemens vertical motor be cleaned and baked?
results.expected_answer: With a quick-drying solvent and lint-free cloths, or low-pressure steam; then oven-bake the whole stator at 200°F for 12 hours and then 230°F for 12 hours
results.rewritten_query: What are the cleaning and baking procedures for MICLAD VPI stator coils on Siemens vertical motors?
results.answer:
To clean MICLAD VPI stator coils on a Siemens vertical motor, follow these steps:

1. **Initial Cleaning**: 
   - Use a quick drying solvent and lint-free cloths to wipe down the coils. Alternatively, you may steam clean with low-pressure steam.

2. **Oven Baking**:
   - After initial cleaning, oven bake the entire stator according to the following schedule:
     - First baking phase at **200°F for 12 hours**.
     - Second baking phase at **230°F for 12 hours**.

3. **Insulation Resistance Check**:
   - Measure the stator winding insulation resistance **before and after** any cleaning operation.

4. **Cleaning Alternatives**:
   - Water and detergents **with an oven drying cycle** may be used as an alternate method for cleaning MICLAD™ VPI insulation systems, assuming compatibility with the insulation system.

These procedures ensure safe and effective maintenance of the stator coils, helping prevent overheating or insulation breakdown caused by debris buildup during operation. The detailed cleaning protocol is outlined in the manufacturer's maintenance guidelines [1].

results.question: How should the re-greasing interval of an ABB machine's rolling bearings change with bearing temperature, and what is the minimum re-greasing frequency?
results.expected_answer: Intervals assume 70°C (160°F); halve them for every 15°C (30°F) increase, and they may be doubled once for a 15°C decrease; re-grease at least once per year regardless
results.rewritten_query: What is the recommended re-greasing interval for rolling bearings in an ABB machine based on bearing temperature, and what is the minimum re-greasing frequency?
results.answer:
The re-greasing interval of an ABB machine's rolling bearings changes with bearing temperature as follows:

- **For every 15°C (30°F) increase in bearing temperature**, the re-greasing interval should be halved.
- **For every 15°C (30°F) decrease in bearing temperature**, the re-greasing interval may be doubled.

Additionally, regardless of the calculated intervals, the bearings must be re-greased **at least once per year** [1]. 

### Summary of Temperature Effects on Re-greasing Intervals
| Temperature Change                  | Re-greasing Interval Change                |
|-------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|
| Increase of 15°C (30°F)            | Halve the re-greasing interval             |
| Decrease of 15°C (30°F)            | May double the re-greasing interval        |

### Minimum Re-greasing Frequency
- Bearings must be re-greased at least **once per year** [1].

contexts:
[1] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 85 · 7.5.3.3 Re-greasing intervals
Rolling bearings of electrical machines need to be re-greased at regular intervals. The re-greasing interval is found on the bearing plate.
NOTE:
Regardless of the re-greasing interval, the bearings need to be re-greased at least once per year.
The re-greasing intervals are calculated for an operating temperature of 70°C (160°F). If the operating temperature is lower or higher than the assumed, the re-grease interval has to be altered accordingly. Higher operating temperature decreases the re-greasing interval.
NOTE:
An increase in the ambient temperature raises the temperature of the bearings correspondingly. The values for the re-greasing interval should be halved for every 15°C (30°F) increase in bearing temperature and may be once doubled for a 15°C (30°F) decrease in bearing temperature.

[2] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 86 · Automatic re-greasing
A variety of automatic re-lubrication systems is available on the market. However, ABB recommends only the use of electromechanical re-lubrication systems. The quality of the grease entering the bearing has to be checked at least once per year: the grease has to look and feel like new grease. Any separation of the base oil from the soap is not acceptable.
NOTE:
If an automatic re-greasing system is used, double the amount of grease indicated on the bearing plate.

[3] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 86 · 7.5.3.5 Bearing grease (table)
It is essential to use grease of good quality and with the correct base soap. This will ensure a long and trouble free lifetime of the bearings.
Grease used for re-greasing should have the following properties:
- Be special rolling bearing grease.
- Be of good quality with a lithium complex soap, and with mineral-, or PAO-oil.
- Have a base oil viscosity of 100 to 160 cSt at 40°C (105°F).
- Have a consistency NLGI grade between 1.5 and 3. For vertically or in hot conditions mounted machines, NLGI grade 2 or 3 is recommended.
- Have a continuous temperature range between -30°C (-20°F) and at least +120°C (250°F).
Grease with the correct properties is available from all major lubricant manufacturers. If the make of grease is changed and compatibility is uncertain, consult the manufacturing ABB factory, see Chapter 9.1.3 Contact information for Motors and Generators Service.
| NOTE: | Do not mix greases! There must be only one type of grease inside the bearing - not a mixture of two or more greases. |
| - | - |
| NOTE: | Grease additives are recommended. However, a written guarantee should be obtained from the lubricant manufacturer stating that the additives do not damage the bearings or the properties of the grease in the field of the operating temperature. This is especially important for EP additives. |
| NOTE: | Lubricants containing EP admixtures are not recommended. |

[4] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 85 · 7.5.3.4 Re-greasing
All rolling bearings of rotating electrical machines need to be re-greased, see Chapter 7.5.3.3 Re-greasing intervals. The re-greasing can be performed either manually or by means of an automatic system. In either case, it has to be verified that a suitable amount of the correct grease is entering the bearing at suitable intervals.
NOTE:
Grease can cause skin irritation and eye inflammation. Follow all safety precautions specified by the grease manufacturer.

[5] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 87 · 7.5.3.6 Bearing maintenance
The lifetime of the bearings is likely to be shorter than the lifetime of the electrical machine. Therefore, the bearings will have to be changed periodically.
The maintenance of rolling bearings requires special care, tools and arrangements as to ensure a long lifetime of newly fitted bearings.
During bearing maintenance, ensure that:
- No dirt or foreign debris is allowed to enter the bearings at any time during the maintenance.
- The bearings are washed, dried and pre-greased with suitable and high quality rolling bearing grease before assembly.
- The disassembly and mounting of the bearings does not damage the bearings. The bearings must be removed by using pullers and fitted by heating, or using special tools for the purpose.
If there is a need to change bearings, please contact ABB Motors and Generators Service. See Motors and Generators contact information in Chapter 9.1.3 Contact information for Motors and Generators Service.

results.question: After manually re-greasing an ABB machine while it is running, how long should it keep running?
results.expected_answer: 1–2 hours, so excess grease is forced out of the bearing (bearing temperature may rise temporarily)
results.rewritten_query: After manually re-greasing an ABB machine while in operation, how long should the machine continue to run safely?
results.answer:
After manually re-greasing an ABB machine while it is running, it should keep running for **1-2 hours** to ensure that all excess grease is forced out of the bearing. During this time, it is normal for the bearing temperature to temporarily increase. 

### Procedure for Manual Re-greasing While Running:
1. Verify that the grease to be used is suitable.
2. Clean the grease nipples and the area around them.
3. Verify that the lubrication channel is open; if equipped with a handle, open it.
4. Press the specified amount and type of grease into the bearing.
5. Let the machine run for **1-2 hours**.
6. If equipped with a handle, close it.

### Additional Notes:
- Beware of all rotating parts during the re-greasing process. [1]

If an automatic re-greasing system is used, double the amount of grease indicated on the bearing plate.

[4] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 85 · 7.5.3.4 Re-greasing
All rolling bearings of rotating electrical machines need to be re-greased, see Chapter 7.5.3.3 Re-greasing intervals. The re-greasing can be performed either manually or by means of an automatic system. In either case, it has to be verified that a suitable amount of the correct grease is entering the bearing at suitable intervals.
NOTE:
Grease can cause skin irritation and eye inflammation. Follow all safety precautions specified by the grease manufacturer.

[5] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 118 · 9.2.1 General spare part considerations
The machines manufactured by ABB are designed and manufactured to provide reliable and trouble-free operation for decades. This requires, however, that the machines are properly maintained and operated. This maintenance includes changing of parts subjected to normal wear.
There is always an inevitable amount of uncertainty related to wearing. The wear rates of these parts vary greatly according to application, environment and particular conditions. Therefore, the condition of these parts should be inspected regularly and a sufficient amount of spare parts should be kept in stock. These spares help to minimize down time if the need appears. The extent of the stock should be decided based upon the criticality of the application, the availability of the particular spare part and the recommendation of the manufacturer.

[2] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 114 · 8.3.2 Pt-100 resistance temperature detectors
Pt-100 resistance temperature detectors are an essential part in the machine's condition monitoring and protection system. They are used to measure temperatures in the windings, bearings and in the cooling air. The Pt-100 detector uses a fine platinum filament for the temperature measurement, which can be damaged e.g. by incorrect handling or excessive vibration.
The following symptoms might suggest a problem in a Pt-100 detector:
- Infinite or zero resistance over the detector
- Disappearance of measurement signal during, or after start up
- A significantly different resistance value in a single detector.
If a Pt-100 failure is suspected the findings should always be confirmed from the connection box, by measuring the resistance at the detector with its cables disconnected. The findings should by registered. For the correct measuring current see the appropriate Pt-100 detector. For resistance values at different temperatures, see Table 11 Temperature values for Pt-100 elements.

results.question: On a rigidly mounted ABB machine, which RMS vibration velocity separates zone B from zone C?
results.rewritten_query: What is the RMS vibration velocity threshold that separates zone B from zone C for a rigidly mounted ABB machine?
results.answer:
The RMS vibration velocity that separates zone B from zone C for a rigidly mounted ABB machine is 4.5 mm/s. 

This can be summarized in a table:

| Support Class | Zone Boundary | R.m.s. Velocity [mm/s] |
| - | - | - |
| Rigid | B/C | 4.5 |

### Likely Causes or Reasoning
- Vibration levels exceeding 4.5 mm/s may indicate misalignment, imbalance, or mechanical looseness, which could necessitate maintenance actions.

### Procedure
1. Measure the RMS vibration velocity of the machine using appropriate monitoring equipment.
2. Compare the measured velocity with the threshold value of 4.5 mm/s.
3. If the vibration exceeds 4.5 mm/s:
   - Investigate for potential causes such as misalignment, imbalance, or mechanical looseness.
   - Schedule remedial actions for the machine to bring vibration levels back to acceptable limits.

This procedure ensures the machine operates reliably and avoids transitioning into a state that could lead to further damage. [1]

results.question: whats the lowest insulation resistance thats ok for a used stator winding on an ABB motor
results.rewritten_query: What is the minimum acceptable insulation resistance for a used stator winding in an ABB motor?
results.answer:
The lowest insulation resistance that is acceptable for a used stator winding on an ABB motor is greater than 100 megohms (MΩ) under the condition that the measurement is conducted at 40 °C for 1 to 10 minutes. 

### Further Considerations
- If the insulation resistance values are not reached, potential reasons include:
  - Excess humidity
  - Dirtiness of the insulation
  - Incorrect transportation and storage conditions
  - Incorrect operation of the machine

### Measurement Procedure
1. Ensure the machine has been powered off and is safe to work on.
2. Use an appropriate insulation resistance tester.
3. Apply a test voltage of at least 500 volts but not exceeding the motor's rated voltage.
4. Measure the insulation resistance of the stator winding and ensure the value exceeds 100 MΩ.
5. If the measurement indicates a low resistance, investigate the causes mentioned above.
6. After measurement, briefly earth the windings to avoid electric shock risk.

The guidelines provided can be found in ABB documentation, noting the specific section on insulation resistance [1][4].

[1] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 92 · 7.6.4.3 Minimum values for insulation resistance
Criteria for windings in a normal condition:
Generally, the insulation resistance values for dry windings should exceed the minimum values significantly. Definite values are impossible to give, because resistance varies depending on the machine type and local conditions. In addition, the insulation resistance is affected by the age and usage of the machine. Therefore, the following values can only be considered as guidelines.
The insulation resistance limits, which are given below, are valid at 40 °C, and when the test voltage has been applied for 1 minute or longer.
- Rotor.
For induction machines with wound rotors: R(1-10 min at 40 °C) > 5 MΩ.
NOTE:
- Stator.
For new stators: R(1-10 min at 40 °C) > 1000 MΩ. If the measuring conditions are extremely warm and humid, R(1-10 min at 40 °C) values above 100 MΩ can be accepted.
For used stators: R(1-10 min at 40 °C) > 100 MΩ.
NOTE:
If the values given here are not reached, the reason for the low insulation resistance should be determined. A low insulation resistance value is often caused by excess humidity or dirt, although the actual insulation is intact.

[2] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 18 · Insulation Resistance
Check insulation resistance periodically. Use a hand cranked or solid state insulation resistance tester and test with at least 500 volts, but not greater than motor rated voltage.
For motors with newer insulation systems such as MICLAD™ VPI, the insulation resistance after one minute should be greater than 1000 megohms. (Values in excess of 5000 megohms are common.) For older motors, the minimum value recommended in IEEE Standard 43 can be used. The value in megohms, when corrected to 40°C, is equal to the motor rated voltage in kilovolts plus 1. For example, for a motor with a rated voltage of 2300 volts, the limit value would be:
2.3 + 1 = 3.3 (megohms).

[3] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 10 · Insulation Resistance
Check insulation resistance prior to connecting motor to power supply. A hand cranked or solid state electronic insulation resistance tester, at least 500 volts d.c., but not over rated voltage, is usually used (see Maintenance).
See IEEE Recommended Practice for Testing Insulation Resistance Rotating Machinery IEEE Std 43.

[4] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 90 · 7.6.4 Insulation resistance test
During general maintenance work and before the machine is started up for the first time or after a long period of standstill, the insulation resistance of stator and rotor windings must be measured.
The insulation resistance measurement provides information about the humidity and dirtiness of the insulation. Based upon this information, correct cleaning and drying actions can be determined.
For new machines with dry windings, the insulation resistance is very high. The resistance can, however, be extremely low if the machine has been subjected to incorrect transportation and storage conditions and humidity, or if the machine is operated incorrectly.
NOTE:
Windings should be earthed briefly immediately after measurement in order to avoid risk of electric shock.

[5] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 94 · 7.6.5 Insulation resistance measurement for auxiliaries
To ensure correct operation of the machines protections and other auxiliaries, their condition can be determined by an insulation resistance test. The procedure is described in detail in Chapter 7.6 Maintenance of stator and rotor windings. The test voltage for the space heater should be 500 VDC and for other auxiliaries 100 VDC. The insulation resistance measurement for Pt-100 detectors or proximity probes is not recommended.

results.question: Roughly how many direct-on-line starts per year is an ABB induction machine designed for?
results.rewritten_query: What is the maximum number of direct-on-line starts per year recommended for ABB induction machines?
results.answer:
Roughly, an ABB induction machine is designed for a maximum of 1000 direct-on-line starts per year in a typical application.

### Reasoning
- The number of allowed consecutive starts depends on factors like load characteristics, machine type, design, and the conditions under which the machine is operated. High or frequent starting stresses can lead to elevated temperatures, accelerating aging and potentially causing machine failure. [1]
  
### Procedure for Determining Allowed Starts
1. **Assess Load Characteristics:**
   - Review the torque curve vs. rotational speed and machine inertia.
  
2. **Consult Technical Documents:**
   - Reference the machine's technical documents for specific allowed sequential starts.

3. **Monitor Temperature Conditions:**
   - Ensure that the machine has cooled to ambient temperature (cold start) or operating temperature (warm start) before attempting a new starting sequence. [3]

4. **Implement a Counter System:**
   - Use a counter system to track the number of starts and plan maintenance intervals based on equivalent operating hours. [1] 

5. **Determine Maintenance Needs:**
   - Regularly evaluate the machine's performance and condition based on the number of starts to plan necessary maintenance to avoid premature failure.

This chapter presents a recommended maintenance program for ABB machines. This maintenance program is of a general nature, and should be considered as a minimum level of maintenance. Maintenance should be intensified when local conditions are demanding or very high reliability is required. It should also be noted that even when following this maintenance program, normal supervision and observation of the machine's condition is required.
Please note that even though the maintenance programs below have been customized to match the machine, it might contain references to accessories not available on all machines.
The maintenance program is based on four levels of maintenance, which rotate according to operating hours. The amount of work and down time vary, so that level 1 includes mainly quick visual inspections and level 4 more demanding measurements and replacements. More information about the spare part packages suitable for these maintenances can be found in Chapter 9.2 Spare parts for rotating electrical machines. The recommended maintenance interval can be seen in Table 6 Maintenance intervals. The operation hour recommendation in this chapter is given as equivalent operating hours (Eq. h), that can be counted by the following formula:

The machines manufactured by ABB are designed and manufactured to provide reliable and trouble-free operation for decades. This requires, however, that the machines are properly maintained and operated. This maintenance includes changing of parts subjected to normal wear.
There is always an inevitable amount of uncertainty related to wearing. The wear rates of these parts vary greatly according to application, environment and particular conditions. Therefore, the condition of these parts should be inspected regularly and a sufficient amount of spare parts should be kept in stock. These spares help to minimize down time if the need appears. results.question: For ABB flood-lubricated sleeve bearings, what oil feed pressure is considered normal?
results.rewritten_query: What is the normal oil feed pressure for ABB flood-lubricated sleeve bearings?
results.answer:
The normal supply pressure for ABB flood-lubricated sleeve bearings is 125 kPa ± 25 kPa (18 psi ± 4 psi) [4]. 

### Reasoning
This pressure ensures the right flow of oil to the bearing. Using higher supply pressure does not provide additional benefits and may lead to oil leakages [4].

### Procedure
1. Adjust the oil supply pressure using the pressure valve and orifice.
2. Monitor the supply pressure to maintain it within the normal range of 100 kPa to 150 kPa (14 psi to 22 psi).

### Conditions to Check
- Ensure the oil flow is adequately maintained.
- Check for any signs of oil leakage associated with higher pressures.

The oil level of a self-lubricated sleeve bearing needs to be checked regularly. The correct oil level is in the middle of the oil sight glass, but as long as the oil level is within the oil sight glass, the level is acceptable.
If necessary, refill with suitable lubricant, see Chapter 7.5.2.4 Oil qualities.
The correct oil level of a flood-lubricated sleeve bearing is the same as for a self-lubricated bearing. In floodlubricated bearings, the oil sight glass might be exchanged for an oil outlet flange.

[3] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 83 · 7.5.2 Lubrication of sleeve bearings
The machines are equipped with sleeve bearings with a very long service life provided that the lubrication functions continuously and that the oil type and quality are as per ABB recommendations, and that the oil change instructions are followed.

[4] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 66 · 5.7.3.2 Machines with sleeve bearings
Verify that no rotating parts rub against any stationary parts. Verify through the oil sight glass that the oil level inside bearing is correct. The correct oil level is in the middle of the oil sight glass, but as long as the oil level is within the oil sight glass, the level is acceptable.
Check the temperature and the oil level of the bearings continuously in the beginning. This is particularly important for self-lubricating bearings. If the temperature of the bearing suddenly rises, the machine should be stopped immediately, and the reason for the temperature rise must be found before the machine is re-started. If no logical reason is found from the measurement equipment, it is recommended that the bearing is opened, and its condition verified. If the machine is under warranty, the manufacturing factory must always be contacted before any action is taken.
For self-lubricating bearings, the rotation of the oil ring is verified through the inspection window on top of the bearing. If the oil ring is not rotating, the machine must be stopped immediately, as a stopped oil ring will result in bearing failure.
For flood-lubricated machines, the oil supply pressure is adjusted with the pressure valve and orifice. The normal supply pressure is 125 kPa ± 25 kPa (18 psi ± 4 psi). This gives the right flow of oil to the bearing. Using higher supply pressure gives no additional benefit, but can cause bearing oil leakages. The rate of oil flow is also specified on the dimensional drawing.
NOTE:

In normal operating conditions, sleeve bearings require little maintenance. To ensure reliable operation, the oil level and the amount of oil leakage should be regularly checked.

results.question: ABB class F stator - minimum PI?
results.rewritten_query: What is the minimum insulation resistance (PI) for an ABB class F stator?
results.answer:
The minimum polarization index (PI) value for class F stator windings is more than 2 [1]. 

### Reasoning
- A polarization index value indicates the condition of windings, with values close to 1 suggesting that the windings are humid and dirty. A PI value higher than 2 is generally considered acceptable for class F stator windings.

### Additional Considerations
- If the polarization index falls below the minimum acceptable level, it is essential to investigate potential causes which could include:
  - Excess humidity
  - Dirt accumulation

### Measurement Conditions
- The testing conditions that impact the polarization index include:
  - The necessity of performing the test at temperatures below 50ºC (122ºF) to avoid unpredictable changes in the results due to temperature effects [1]. 

In summary, ensure that the PI for class F stator windings remains above 2 to ensure safe operation.

[1] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 94 · 7.6.6 The polarization index
For the polarization index test the insulation resistance is measured after the voltage has been applied for 15 seconds and 1 minute (or 1 minute and 10 minutes). The polarization index test is less dependent on the temperature than the insulation resistance. When the winding temperature is below 50ºC (122ºF), it may be considered independent of temperature. High temperatures can cause unpredictable changes in the polarization index, therefore the test should not be used at temperatures above 50ºC (122ºF).
Dirt and humidity accumulating in the winding normally reduces the insulation resistance, and the polarization index, as well as their dependence on temperature. Thus, the line in Figure 38 Correlation between the insulation resistance and the temperature becomes less steep. Windings with open creepage distances are very sensitive to the effects of dirt and humidity.
There are several rules for determining the lowest acceptable value with which the machine can be safely started. For the polarization index (PI), the values usually range between 1 and 4. Values close to 1 indicate that the windings are humid and dirty.
The minimum PI value for class F stator windings is more than 2.
NOTE:
<!-- formula-not-decoded -->

Figures for this passage:
- Figure 38 Correlation between the insulation resistance and the temperature — image path: diagrams/fdb5c8bb-ba46-40f5-b9a2-e30841e3a2b4/fig38_1.png

[2] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 92 · 7.6.4.3 Minimum values for insulation resistance
Criteria for windings in a normal condition:
Generally, the insulation resistance values for dry windings should exceed the minimum values significantly. Definite values are impossible to give, because resistance varies depending on the machine type and local conditions. In addition, the insulation resistance is affected by the age and usage of the machine. Therefore, the following values can only be considered as guidelines.
The insulation resistance limits, which are given below, are valid at 40 °C, and when the test voltage has been applied for 1 minute or longer.
- Rotor.
For induction machines with wound rotors: R(1-10 min at 40 °C) > 5 MΩ.
NOTE:
- Stator.
For new stators: R(1-10 min at 40 °C) > 1000 MΩ. If the measuring conditions are extremely warm and humid, R(1-10 min at 40 °C) values above 100 MΩ can be accepted.
For used stators: R(1-10 min at 40 °C) > 100 MΩ.
NOTE:
If the values given here are not reached, the reason for the low insulation resistance should be determined. A low insulation resistance value is often caused by excess humidity or dirt, although the actual insulation is intact.

[3] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 94 · 7.6.5 Insulation resistance measurement for auxiliaries
To ensure correct operation of the machines protections and other auxiliaries, their condition can be determined by an insulation resistance test. The procedure is described in detail in Chapter 7.6 Maintenance of stator and rotor windings. The test voltage for the space heater should be 500 VDC and for other auxiliaries 100 VDC. The insulation resistance measurement for Pt-100 detectors or proximity probes is not recommended.

[4] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 92 · 7.6.4.4 Stator winding insulation resistance measurement
The insulation resistance is measured using an insulation resistance meter. The test voltage is 1000 VDC. The test time is 1 minute, after which the insulation resistance value is recorded. Before the insulation resistance test is conducted, the following actions must be taken:
- Check that the secondary connections of the current transformers (CT's), including spare cores are not open. See Figure 39 Connections of the stator windings for insulation resistance measurements.
- Verify that all power supply cables are disconnected.
- Verify that the frame of the machine and the stator windings not being tested are earthed.
- The winding temperature is measured.
- All resistance temperature detectors are earthed.
- Possible earthing of voltage transformers (not common) must be removed.
The insulation resistance measuring should be carried out in the terminal box. The test is usually performed to the whole winding as a group, in which case the meter is connected between the frame of the machine and the winding; See Figure 39 Connections of the stator windings for insulation resistance measurements. The frame is earthed and the three phases of the stator winding remain connected at the neutral point, see Figure 39 Connections of the stator windings for insulation resistance measurements.
If the measured insulation resistance of the whole winding is lower than specified, and the phase windings can easily be disconnected from each other, each phase can also be measured separately. This is not possible for all machines. In this measurement, the tester is connected between the frame of the machine and one of the windings. The frame and the two phases not measured are earthed; see Figure 39 Connections of the stator windings for insulation resistance measurements.
Carbon dust on slip rings and naked copper surfaces lower the insulation resistance values of the rotor.
When phases are measured separately, all star-points of the winding system must be removed. If the star-point of the component cannot be removed, as in a typical tri-phase voltage transformer, the whole component must be removed.
Figure 39 Connections of the stator windings for insulation resistance measurements
- a) Insulation resistance measurement for star connected winding.
- b) Insulation resistance measurement for delta connected winding.
- c) Insulation resistance measurement for one phase of the winding. The 'MΩ' represents the insulation resistance meter.
After the insulation resistance measurement the winding phases must be earthed briefly in order to discharge them.
Following chapter for rotor type: Slip rings

results.question: What contact pressure should the slip-ring brushes on an ABB machine press with?
results.rewritten_query: What is the recommended contact pressure for slip-ring brushes on an ABB machine?
results.answer:
The slip-ring brushes on an ABB machine should press with a contact pressure of 18-20 mN/mm² (180-200 g/cm²) [1]. 

### Reasoning and Procedure
To ensure proper brush operation, follow these steps:

1. **Use a spring balance**: Attach a spring balance to the tip of the lever pressing the brush.
2. **Measure the pressure**: Pull the balance in a radial direction until the pressure is just relieved from the brush.
3. **Detect pressure relief**: Use a piece of paper between the brush and press lever to identify when the brush pressure is relieved.

This procedure helps confirm that the brush pressure is evenly distributed and within the specified range, which is crucial for optimal functioning [1].

[1] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 95 · 7.7.2.1 Brush pressure
The brush pressure should be evenly distributed over the whole contact surface, i.e. the brush should conform to the slip ring curvature. Brush pressure is one of the most important single factors in brush operation. The pressure should be 18-20 mN/mm2 (180-200 g/cm2). Use a spring-balance to measure the brush pressure. Attach a spring balance to the tip of the lever pressing the brush and pull in a radial direction until the pressure is just relieved from the brush. Use a piece of paper between brush and press lever to detect when pressure is relieved, see Figure 41 Checking brush pressure with spring balance.
Figure 41 Checking brush pressure with spring balance

Figures for this passage:
- Figure 41 Checking brush pressure with spring balance — image path: diagrams/fdb5c8bb-ba46-40f5-b9a2-e30841e3a2b4/fig41_1.png

[2] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 96 · 7.7.3 Care of carbon dust filter
The slip ring unit of the permanent contact type is equipped with filter for carbon dust. The cleaning interval of the filter in respect to carbon brush wear is shown in Figure 42 Maximum cleaning interval of the slip ring housing carbon dust filter, parameter brush wear in mm/10³ h.
The slip ring housing is equipped with a differential pressure switch for monitoring the condition of the filters. The filter must be changed immediately after an alarm. It is also highly recommended that the operating personnel manually inspects the filters frequently.
The carbon dust filter can be cleaned by washing, beating, or spraying.
Figure 42 Maximum cleaning interval of the slip ring housing carbon dust filter, parameter brush wear in mm/10³ h

Figures for this passage:
- Figure 42 Maximum cleaning interval of the slip ring housing carbon dust filter, parameter brush wear in mm/10³ h — image path: diagrams/fdb5c8bb-ba46-40f5-b9a2-e30841e3a2b4/fig42_1.png

[3] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 115 · 8.4.1 Brush wear
In case the brushes are wearing rapidly or unevenly, the following points shall be observed:
- Is the brush pressure within the specified range? See Chapter 7.7.2.1 Brush pressure.
- Are all brush pigtail cables reliably connected?
- Are the sliding surfaces of the slip rings deteriorated?
- Is it probable that carbon brushes have absorbed oil or moisture?
- Is the brush quality as specified for the machine?
Always when feasible:
- Control that the brushes are in good condition and that they can move freely in the brush holders
- Check that the brush pigtail cables are in order and that they are reliably connected
- Remove coal dust by vacuum cleaning.

[4] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 96 · 7.7.4 Care of brush lifting device
The slip ring assembly and slip ring housing shall be checked at regular service intervals.
For brush lifting device, control the movement to be set and the contacts to be corrected every six months or 100 starts.

[5] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 94 · 7.7.1 Care of slip rings
The sliding surfaces of the slip rings should be kept smooth and clean. The slip rings should be inspected and the surfaces of the insulation cleaned. Wearing of brushes produces coal dust that easily builds up conducting bridges over the insulation surfaces. Electric discharges may take place between slip rings and a flash might appear, leading to interruption in operation of the machine. The contact surface of slip rings forms a patina, or skin, together with the brushes. The patina can be seen as a colored surface, it is normal behavior and in many cases a benefit to brush operation, so the patina is not be considered as a fault in operation and should not be cleared away.
If the insulation resistance of the winding is in the range of several thousands of MΩ, the polarization index is not a meaningful criterion of the condition of the insulation, and it can be disregarded.

results.question: Which DC voltage should I megger an ABB motor's space heater at?
results.rewritten_query: What is the recommended DC voltage for megger testing the space heater of an ABB motor?
results.answer:
To megger an ABB motor's space heater, you should use a test voltage of **500 VDC** [2]. 

Here is the procedure for conducting the insulation resistance measurement:

1. Gather your insulation resistance testing equipment (a DC insulation resistance tester).
2. Set the tester to apply **500 VDC** for the space heater.
3. Connect the tester leads to the space heater terminals.
4. Initiate the test and record the insulation resistance value.
5. Compare the recorded value against acceptable standards for operation.

The test voltage for the space heater specifically is provided, and it is important to follow this guideline to ensure accurate measurements and compliance with safety standards.
